Cleanup Underway After Violent Clashes Rock Mendiola-Recto in Manila..

#Manila, #Philippines Personnel from the Manila City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO) and the Department of Public Services (DPS) were deployed Sunday to clear Recto Avenue following the chaos that erupted overnight.
The Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) and Canine Unit of the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO), along with the Manila Police District (MPD), are also processing evidence in front of a hotel where a violent commotion broke out after a group of men stormed the area.
Several protesters and police officers were injured during the disturbance at Mendiola-Recto and were rushed to nearby hospitals for treatment.
Manila City Mayor Isko Moreno praised the swift response of the police in handling the situation, while strongly condemning the unruly individuals who vandalized government property during the rally.
Mayor Moreno also ordered all loitering minors to return home ahead of the city-wide 10 p.m., In addition, he directed authorities to immediately remove debris and damaged items left behind by the rioters in Mendiola.

data.raw_text:
Violence erupted in Manila, the Philippines  on September 21 during several mass rallies against corruption, after protesters were barred by police from marching to the presidential palace.

Protesters threw rocks and Molotov cocktails at anti-riot police, while security forces used flash bangs and water cannons to disperse the demonstrators.

Dozens of protesters wore masks and carried a flag from the Japanese manga series "One Piece", reminiscent of the symbol used during recent violent protests in Indonesia.

The Philippine National Police has reported dozens of injuries, mostly from cuts and bruises, and said it has arrested 17 protesters involved in the clash.

WATCH: The mother of an apprehended protester—whose video of them being throw around by the police at Mendiola, Sunday afternoon, circulated on social media—is in tears as she waits outside the Manila Police Department UN Headquarters.

Though she was told that police readied first aid for injured individuals who were arrested, she still asked that she be allowed to take her child for a CT scan or, at the very least, see her child at all.

"Sana may makausap kaming matino sa kanila (Manila Police Department). Lahat kaming magulang andito para sa peace of mind ...  at para malaman kung ano ang gagawin namin," she said.
